name: Tatar
notes:
Tatar in Cyrillic script (Tatarstan). Nine vowels with front/back harmony: а /ɑ/, ә /æ/, о /o/, ө /ø/, у /u/, ү /y/, ы /ɯ/, и /i/, е /e/. The low pair а/ә and the high-back ы are given the values Comrie (1997) assigns them in his phonemic inventory of Kazan Tatar (open back unrounded /ɑ/, open front unrounded /æ/, close back unrounded /ɯ/); Comrie's own chapter was not obtained this session, so the inventory is verified against Table 3.2 of Henry (2018), a fetched paper that reproduces it in full and cites Comrie as its source. The remaining vowel/consonant values follow Berta (1998), "Tatar and Bashkir", in The Turkic Languages, Johanson & Csató eds. (edition not consulted this session; standard Turkological description). Я, being й+а, is /jɑ/ for the same reason. Ә, Ө, Ү are Cyrillic letters with descenders/hooks, not the Latin ə ö ü they resemble.

Tatar Cyrillic has no distinct letter for the uvular fricative/stop: г spells both /ɡ/ and /ʁ/, and к both /k/ and /q/, conditioned by front/back vowel harmony (Berta 1998). The convention that marks the back (uvular) reading is the digraphs ⟨гъ⟩ and ⟨къ⟩ (ъ after г/к signals /ʁ/, /q/ rather than its own glottal value); that digraph rule is left unmodeled here — г and к are given their plain (front-harmony) values only, and ъ/ь keep their independent glottal candidate below regardless of context. This is a documented residual pending a primary-source wave, not a silent deletion, since г/к still surface as segments.

Җ is a Tatar-specific letter, the voiced alveolo-palatal fricative /ʑ/, distinct from Ж /ʒ/ (Berta 1998). Ң = /ŋ/, Һ = /h/.

Ъ and Ь mark [ʔ] (glottal stop/glottalization); no fetched primary source describes this convention explicitly, so it rests on a distributional argument rather than a citation: every ъ-word (106/106) and every ь-word (439/439) in the vox_communis benchmark's gold carries ʔ (see tests/test_tatar.py). A silent reading is kept as a secondary candidate for the minority of tokens where they are orthographic-only. Ё /jo/ and Ц /ts/, Щ /ʃtʃ/, В /v/ carry Russian loanwords; unassimilated Russian loans commonly break front/back vowel harmony within one word (measured at roughly 11% of word types in the vox_communis wordlist), which is orthographically harmless here since а/ә/о/ө/у/ү/ы are already distinct letters independent of harmony class.

stress.notes: Tatar default stress is word-final (-1). Certain suffixes (negation, question particle) and borrowed words carry non-final stress; lexical and not modeled here. Source: Comrie (1997), Johanson & Csató (1998).
